confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from five web searches that returned aggregated cost-of-living sources (MyLifeElsewhere, Traveltables, Expat Arrivals, Expatistan-style listings and travel guides). These sources are crowdsourced, differ from one another, and some are dated. Restaurant-meal ranges were fairly consistent, at roughly $3-5 for an inexpensive meal and $25-37 for a mid-range meal for two. Beer is around $2-3 and a cappuccino around $2.5. I set beer at the upper end of the aggregates because the anchor is a restaurant serving, not a shop price. Cocktail is based on pisco sour prices of about 18-35 PEN in tourist and bar settings. No reliable per-glass wine price was found, so the wine anchor is derived from the local price relationship to beer and a mid-range bottle of about 35 PEN. Both drink anchors are therefore less certain. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation returned by the single FX search. That search also returned some older or inconsistent cached RBA pages, which I did not use. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Lima's tourist districts such as Miraflores and Barranco. No accommodation searches or live listings were used, so these carry the most uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lima is priced against its own aggregated local data. Its price level is similar to other mid-cost Andean and Latin American capitals such as Bogotá and Quito, with tourist-district prices (Miraflores, Barranco) somewhat above local averages.
